items.label: Audit update — August 3, 2026
items.text: re-audited against the current Team Stores Workspace prototype. The Settings tab now uses a six-section left sub-nav (previously a two-section pill nav): General, Schedule & Status, Team & Roster, People & Access, Distribution & Fulfillment, and Catalog & Decoration (only when a third-party vendor is enabled for the store). League/Team Manager Information moved into General; team-manager portal invites moved out of Distribution into the new People & Access section; Distribution & Fulfillment is now only the fulfillment method plus the team-manager order-fulfillment mapping. Rewritten August 24, 2026 following the team store testing walkthrough: the Store Point of Contact Service mode is replaced by Team Manager, and the tax State select is searchable. Updated August 25, 2026: Allow Duplicate Numbers becomes a bulk default over per-roster settings, and the Store Close Report is specified (Epic H). Updated August 31, 2026: the ship-to destination address for Ship to Team Manager is editable here (Epic A3); the manager card holds multiple manager records with a designated primary; Team & Roster values can now also be set during store creation; the card previously called "Store Distribution Model" is named the Fulfillment Method card throughout, matching the section table and Step 1. The six-section count in this August 3 note is superseded by the September 2, 2026 amendment below — the sub-nav now carries seven sections.

items.label: Amended September 1, 2026 (a)
items.text: Team Fundraising becomes a store-level master over per-item toggles. Following the removal of Team Profit and the introduction of a per-item fundraising toggle in the price settings component (see Product Catalog Management (Products Tab), Governing rule 3), the Team Fundraising control on the Store Details card is no longer a simple boolean. Disabling it now sweeps the catalog through a confirmation interstitial, cannot override the commercial lock on already-ordered items, and therefore resolves to a three-state read. Specified in the new Epic A4.

items.label: Amended September 1, 2026 (b)
items.text: connect-to-team now imports coach records. The Team Database attaches coach records to its teams and organizations; the connect-to-team component previously pulled only branding, leaving reps to hand-type contact details the platform already held. Coaches are now returned on connect and offered for verification and selection as manager records. Epic A1 covers the behavior on re-bind, which is materially harder than at creation because the store already carries managers, orders, and portal invites. The creation-time flow is owned by Step 1 — Basics, Epic D2.

items.label: Amended September 2, 2026 (c)
items.text: a seventh Settings section, Store Customization & Design, positioned after Team & Roster. It holds the store theme color (defaulting to the connected team's primary color, overridable via the Prolook color picker, applied to buttons and accents only) and the storefront Announcement Message (rich text, rendered per Storefront Announcement Banner). Specified in the new Epic I. The announcement message is also authored during store creation — see Step 1 — Basics, Epic H — and writes the same store-level field this section reads. Both controls are explicitly exempt from post-launch locking (Epic B): a banner whose purpose is communicating deadlines on a live store is useless if it freezes at launch. Storefront theme color was previously treated as post-initial-release and is now in scope, deliberately limited to buttons and accents rather than full theming.

items.label: Amended October 12, 2026 (d)
items.text: the ship-to destination can be chosen from saved Pick-up Locations. Destinations are saved once at workspace level and selected per store rather than typed into each one. Added as a bullet under Epic A3; the locations themselves are owned by Pick Up Locations, and the creation-time equivalent by Step 1 — Basics, Epic F. Manual address entry is unchanged.

items.label: The Problem
items: The settings a rep chooses during store creation (name, web address, format, timeline, branding, contacts, fulfillment, tax) aren't final — names get corrected, dates shift, branding updates, contacts change. Without a place to revisit them, a rep would have to recreate a store to fix a setting. As the tab grew (ordering windows, roster rules, jersey numbers, manager portal access, freight mapping), a two-section split stopped scaling: unrelated concerns shared a page, and store identity sat alongside people management.
A closed store also has no moment of closure. The rep hits their deadline, the storefront locks, and the outcome of weeks of work is left sitting in a reports table nobody opens.

A third gap appeared once fundraising became a per-item decision. A store-level switch that silently rewrites every product in the catalog is a large, invisible action — and one that cannot be allowed to reach items buyers have already paid against.
A fourth: coaching changes are the most common contact edit a rep makes, and until now every one of them was typed by hand even where the Team Database already held the new coach's record.

A fifth, and the reason this tab gains a section: the rep has no way to tell buyers anything. Key dates, order deadlines, returns, sizing, and shipping are the questions parents actually ask, and no field in this tab holds an answer to any of them. Usability research found reps treat store information as setup rather than decoration — they expect somewhere to type it, and there wasn't one.

items.label: The Solution
items: A Settings tab inside the store manager where the rep edits and manages the store's information after creation, organized as a left sub-nav of seven sections. Each section holds read-only cards with their own pencil-edit affordance opening a focused edit modal. Closing a store produces a Store Close Report — a summary presented once, on the rep's next return to the workspace, with a scoped variant for team managers. Disabling Team Fundraising presents the rep with exactly what it will change before it changes it. Re-connecting the store to a team offers that team's coaches as manager records rather than leaving the rep to retype them. Store Customization & Design gives the rep a place to set the storefront's accent color and to write the announcement message buyers read at the top of the store.

Who is this for? The store manager (rep) editing and managing store information after or as a store has been created.

items.label: Scenarios encountered
items.text: Fixing a store name or web address before launch; extending a pop-up's closing deadline or setting per-team-code order windows; swapping the imported team logo/colors; changing the point-of-contact from the team manager to a salesperson; correcting a team manager's phone number and having the storefront footer follow; adding a second coach to the manager list after setup, or promoting one to primary; re-connecting a store bound to the wrong team and pulling the right team's coaches in the same action; adding a mid-season replacement coach who is already in the Team Database rather than typing their details; re-connecting a team and being warned that the manager already invited to the portal came from the old team; entering the bulk-shipment destination address a rep skipped during creation, or correcting one they mistyped; pointing a store at a saved pick-up location instead of retyping the dealership's address; swapping a store from one saved location to another when freight moves; changing the duplicate-number rule that was set during store creation; setting the rule for every team at once and then adjusting one division; deciding who picks jersey numbers; writing the order deadline, return policy, and sizing guidance buyers see at the top of the storefront; updating that deadline mid-window because the mill pushed the production date; giving one division of a league its own deadline while the rest of the league keeps the league-wide message; accepting the team's primary color as the storefront accent, or overriding it with a color the coach asked for; applying a division's own brand color to the storefront for shoppers who select that division; inviting a team manager to the portal and revoking access later; assigning division/team managers for freight routing; turning fundraising off for a whole store and seeing exactly which products it affects before confirming; discovering that two already-ordered items will keep collecting; turning fundraising back on months later and finding every item as it was left; reviewing how a store performed after it closes; sharing a manager-scoped version of that report with a coach; switching the fulfillment method while still in draft; setting art policy on a store that carries a third-party vendor's catalog.

blocks.heading: User Stories
items: As a rep, I want a Settings tab to edit my store's information, so that I can correct or update settings without recreating the store.
As a rep, I want settings grouped by concern in a sub-nav, so that I can find a setting by what it does rather than scrolling one long page.
As a rep, I want each card edited in its own focused modal, so that I can update one area at a time without wading through every field.
As a rep, I want to reconnect the store to a different team, so that I can re-import the correct logo, colors, and sports if it was bound to the wrong team.
As a rep, I want a reconnect to offer me the new team's coaches, so that fixing a wrong team binding doesn't leave me retyping contact details that already exist.
As a rep, I want to pull a coach from the Team Database when the coaching staff changes mid-season, so that a routine personnel change is a selection rather than data entry.

As a rep, I want to be told when a reconnect leaves behind managers from the old team — especially any who have portal access — so that a branding fix doesn't quietly leave the wrong person able to see this store.
As a rep, I want the storefront contact to follow the team manager's record, so that fixing their phone number in one place fixes it everywhere.
As a rep, I want to add or remove managers after setup and control which one is the primary contact, so that a coaching change is an edit rather than a rebuild.
As a rep shipping in bulk, I want to see and edit the destination address in one obvious place, so that a store I launched without one is easy to complete.
As a rep who ships to the same place repeatedly, I want to pick a saved pick-up location rather than retype its address, so that a corrected address is corrected everywhere at once.
As a rep, I want the roster rules I chose during store creation to be exactly what I find here, so that I am not wondering which of two places wins.
As a rep, I want to set the duplicate-number rule across every roster at once, so that per-team control doesn't mean configuring each roster by hand.

As a rep, I want somewhere to write the key dates, deadlines, returns, sizing, and shipping information buyers keep asking me about, so that the answers are on the storefront instead of in my text messages.
As a rep, I want to edit that message on a live store, so that a moved production date is a two-minute fix rather than something I cannot change until the window closes.
As a rep running a league, I want a division to be able to carry its own message, so that one division's different deadline doesn't require me to write a message covering every division at once.
As a rep, I want the storefront to pick up my team's color without my doing anything, and to let me change it when the coach asks, so that the default is right and the override is available.
As a rep, I want a single place to invite and revoke team-manager portal access, so that people management isn't buried in fulfillment settings.
As a rep running a League store that ships to team managers, I want to map a manager to every division or team, so that bulk freight is routed to the right person.
As a rep, I want to see every product I am about to change before I turn fundraising off for the store, so that a one-click switch isn't a blind rewrite of my catalog.
As a rep, I want to be told which items can't have fundraising removed because they've already been ordered, so that I understand why the store isn't fully switched off.
As a rep, I want turning fundraising back on to restore what I had, so that re-enabling isn't a fresh configuration job.
As a rep, I want a summary of how a store performed once it closes, so that the result of the season is a moment rather than a spreadsheet.
As a team manager, I want my own version of that summary covering only my team, so that I can see how we did without seeing the rep's margins.
As a rep, I want to freely edit everything while the store is in draft, so that I can fully dial it in before going live.

blocks.heading: Epic A — Seven-section Settings layout & per-card edit modals
items: The Settings tab renders a sticky left sub-nav (label + one-line description per section); the selected section fills the content area. Each card is read-only with a pencil-edit affordance opening a focused modal; field types and conditional logic mirror Step 1 — Basics of the creation flow. Order: General → Schedule & Status → Team & Roster → Store Customization & Design → People & Access → Distribution & Fulfillment → Catalog & Decoration (conditional).

items.label: General → Store Details card → "Edit Store Details" modal
items.text: Read view shows Store Name, Store Type (Individual Team Store / League Store), Team Name, Sport, boxed Team Logo and Team Colors, plus in-card blocks for Team Fundraising (a three-state pill — see Epic A4) and the Store Point of Contact (Email + Phone channels, each showing its mode and resolved value). The modal edits Store Name, Team Name, Team Branding & Sport (connect-to-team component with coach import, Team Logo drop zone, Team Colors, Sports multi-select), the Roster Rules and Team Fundraising toggles, Compliance & Taxation (Collect Sales Tax toggle; when on, a searchable State select — type-ahead filtering on state name and two-letter postal abbreviation — that auto-fills the read-only flat Tax Rate %), and the Store Point of Contact.

items.label: General → League/Team Manager Information card → edit modal
items.text: Titled League Manager Information for League stores and Team Manager Information for single-team stores. The card holds one or more manager records (see Epic A2c). Each record's read view shows Name, Street Address (street/apt, city, state, ZIP), Phone Number, Email, and Contact Preference (Email/Phone chips), with the primary record marked. This card lives in General — it is the store's contact record of record, not a fulfillment setting. Because the Store Point of Contact can inherit from the primary record (Epic A2), edits there propagate to the storefront footer.

items.label: Schedule & Status
items.text: Active Order Window card → "Edit Store Schedule" modal, plus the Order Window Scheduler and repeating close dates (Epic E). Store Status card → Close / Re-open Store (Epic D), the Create Template action, and the Danger Zone → Archive Store (Epic C). The Store Close Report (Epic H) is reachable from this section once the store has closed.

items.label: Team & Roster
items.text: Roster Rules card (Allow Duplicate Numbers — a bulk default over per-roster settings, see Epic F) and the Jersey Number Selection card (Epic F). Both controls are also surfaced during store creation in Step 1 — Basics, Epic D1; that panel and these cards read and write the same store-level values, so whatever the rep chose at setup is what appears here.

items.label: Store Customization & Design
items.text: The Store Theme Color card and the Announcement Message card (Epic I). On League stores the section additionally lists divisions and standalone teams for per-scope announcement overrides and division-color application. The announcement message is also surfaced during store creation in Step 1 — Basics, Epic H, writing the same store-level value; the theme color is not offered in the wizard.

items.label: People & Access
items.text: Team Manager Access — invites and portal access for this store (Epic A2b).

items.label: Distribution & Fulfillment
items.text: The Fulfillment Method card → its own edit modal (Ship to Team Manager (FREE) vs. Direct-To-Home Residential Delivery, shown with icon, badge, and helper copy, plus the ship-to destination address when Ship to Team Manager is selected — Epic A3), and — for League stores shipping to team managers — the Team Manager & Order Fulfillment Mapping (Epic A3). Nothing else lives here.

items.label: Catalog & Decoration
items.text: Seller scope and art policy — rendered only when a third-party vendor is enabled for the store (Epic G).

blocks.heading: Epic A1 — Connect-to-Team component & coach import
items: The Edit Store Details modal (General) carries a connect-to-team component under Team Branding & Sport, letting the rep bind or re-bind the store to a team profile and pull its official branding and its coach records.

items.label: Connected state
items.text: Given a store bound to a team, when the modal opens, then a banner reads "Connected — [Team Name]" noting the official logo, colors, and sports were imported, with a Change Team action (unbound stores show "Import Team Profile" with a Connect to Team action).

items.label: Reconnect / switch
items.text: Given the connected banner, when the rep clicks Change Team, then they can reconnect to a different team profile via the team-database picker and the Team Logo, Team Colors, and Sports re-import from the newly connected team. The store theme color re-derives on the same action where it is still on the team default — see Epic I.

blocks.heading: Coach import — same model as creation, harder context
items: The Team Database attaches coach records to its teams and organizations. A connect returns those records alongside the branding, and the rep converts the ones they want into manager records on the League/Team Manager Information card (Epic A2c). The selection model is identical to Step 1 — Basics, Epic D2 and is not restated here: nothing is imported silently, records are shown in full for verification, multiple coaches are multi-selectable, and imported records are point-in-time copies that never write back to the Team Database and never live-sync from it.

items.label: What differs after the store exists
The store already has managers
items.text: A connect adds; it never replaces. Given the rep selects coaches from a newly connected team, when they save, then those records are appended to the existing manager collection. No existing record is overwritten, demoted, or deleted as a side effect of a reconnect.

items.label: Re-binding surfaces the managers that came from the old team
items.text: Given the rep re-binds a store to a different team, when the reconnect completes, then the modal lists any existing manager records imported from the previously connected team and asks whether they should be kept or removed. It is a prompt, not an automatic cleanup — a coach may legitimately follow a team, and a rep may have hand-corrected a record until it is right.

items.label: Records carrying portal access are called out separately
items.text: Given one of those managers has an active or pending invite in People & Access (Epic A2b), then the prompt names them and states plainly that removing the manager record does not revoke their portal access, which is a separate action in People & Access. A branding fix must never quietly leave the wrong person able to read this store's reporting and rosters, and it must never silently revoke access the rep did not ask to revoke.

items.label: Hand-entered records are never listed here
items.text: The prompt covers only records whose origin was an import from the team being replaced. A manager the rep typed is theirs and is left alone.

items.label: The primary is protected
items.text: Given the current primary manager record would be removed by the re-bind prompt, when the rep confirms, then removal is blocked until another record is designated primary — the existing rule in Epic A2c applies unchanged. A reconnect can never leave a store with zero managers where a point-of-contact channel depends on one.

items.label: Point-of-contact consequences are stated before saving
items.text: Given a point-of-contact channel is on Team Manager mode, when a reconnect changes which record is primary, then the modal states that the storefront footer will change and shows the resolved values, consistent with Epic A2c's treatment of primary re-designation. This is buyer-visible and is never applied silently.

items.label: A rep does not need to re-bind the store to import a coach
items.text: Given the store is already connected to the correct team, when the rep opens the connect-to-team component, then the current team's coach records are available for selection — so a mid-season staff change is a selection against the team the store is already bound to, not a reconnect.

items.label: OPEN — to be confirmed
items.text: whether this re-fetch should be surfaced on the League/Team Manager Information card as well (e.g. an "Add from Team Database" action beside "Add manager"), which is where a rep looking to add a coach would naturally go, rather than only inside the branding component. Recommend yes; confirm the surface before build.

blocks.heading: Import grants nothing

Team Manager Portal entitlement is created solely by an explicit invite in People & Access (Epic A2b). This rule is absolute and is the single most important constraint on the feature.

blocks.heading: Epic A2b — People & Access (Team Manager Portal invites)
items: As a rep, I want a single place to invite and revoke team-manager portal access, so that people management isn't buried in fulfillment settings.

items.label: Scope copy
items.text: the section explains the invitee lands in a slimmed-down portal with exactly two areas — Reporting and Rosters (no products, orders, settings, or vault) — scoped to this store only.

items.label: Send an invite
items.text: an email field + Send Invite (disabled until the address validates; Enter submits). On send, the invite is added to the table and a toast confirms; helper copy notes the invitee receives an email link to set a Team Manager Portal password.

blocks.heading: Epic A2c — Multiple manager records (General → League/Team Manager Information)
items: As a rep, I want to add or remove managers after setup and control which one is the primary contact, so that a coaching change is an edit rather than a rebuild.

items.label: Origin does not create classes of record
items.text: An imported coach and a hand-typed manager are the same kind of record: same fields, same editability, same eligibility for primary designation, invites, and fulfillment mapping. No downstream consumer distinguishes them.

items.label: Add / remove
items.text: Given the manager card, when the rep opens its modal, then they can add further manager records (First Name, Last Name, Email, Phone Number, Street Address, Contact Preference) and remove any non-primary record.

items.label: Editing an imported record is local
items.text: Given an imported manager record, when the rep corrects a field, then the change applies to this store only and is never written back to the Team Database. Team Stores consumes that data; it does not maintain it.

items.label: Exactly one primary
items.text: Given the collection, then exactly one record is designated primary at all times. The primary is the inheritance source for the Store Point of Contact (Epic A2) and the only record whose contact fields are subject to point-of-contact validation.

items.label: Changing the primary
items.text: Given a non-primary record, when the rep designates it primary, then the previous primary is demoted, and any point-of-contact channel on Team Manager mode immediately resolves to the new primary's value on the storefront footer. items.label: Removing the primary

items.label: Removal and portal access are separate
items.text: Removing a manager record does not revoke a portal invite issued to that person (Epic A2b). Where the record being removed has an active or pending invite, the confirmation says so and links to People & Access.

items.label: Addresses
items.text: every manager record carries an address, used for order fulfillment routing (Epic A3). For a single-manager store shipping to the team manager, that address is the ship-to destination. blocks.heading: Epic A3 — Fulfillment Method, ship-to destination & Order Fulfillment Mapping (Distribution & Fulfillment)
items: As a rep shipping in bulk, I want to see and edit the destination address in one obvious place, so that a store I launched without one is easy to complete.
As a rep who ships to the same place repeatedly, I want to pick a saved pick-up location rather than retype its address, so that a corrected address is corrected everywhere at once.
As a rep running a League store that ships to team managers, I want to map a manager to every division or team, so that bulk freight is routed to the right person.
The Fulfillment Method card owns the store's shipping model and, when that model is bulk, where the bulk shipment goes.

items.label: Method
items.text: Ship to Team Manager (FREE) vs. Direct-To-Home Residential Delivery, mirroring Step 1 — Basics, Epic F.

items.label: Ship-to destination address (conditional — Ship to Team Manager only)
items.text: Given the method is Ship to Team Manager, when the card renders, then it shows the destination address (street/apt, city, state, ZIP) with the card's edit affordance; the rep can edit it or clear it. Given the method is Direct-To-Home, then no destination address is shown.

items.label: Choosing from saved Pick-up Locations
items.text: Given the workspace has saved Pick-up Locations (see Pick Up Locations) and the method is Ship to Team Manager, when the rep edits the destination, then they may either select a saved location or enter a Ship-To Address manually; where no locations exist, manual entry behaves exactly as it does today and the rep is prompted that destinations can be saved once and reused. A selected location is held as a reference, not a copy — an edit to that location in Workspace Settings propagates here with no action, and a location switched off at workspace level leaves this store with no destination, surfaced as the "No destination address" state below and blocked at the freight gate until one is supplied (Pick Up Locations, Epic C). Selecting a location and typing an address write the same destination field; a store has one destination however it was supplied, and the rep can swap between the two input methods freely.

items.label: One address, two surfaces
items.text: This is the same record as the address captured in Step 1 — Basics, Epic F, and the same address held on the store's primary manager record (Epic A2c) — not a third copy. An address entered during creation appears here unchanged, and an edit here is what the freight gate reads. Neither surface holds a value the other cannot see.

items.label: Clearing is permitted, and consequential
items.text: Given the rep clears the destination address, when they save, then the save succeeds and the card shows a "No destination address" state with the consequence stated: pending orders cannot be submitted for fulfillment until an address exists. The clear is not blocked — a rep correcting a wrong address should not have to keep a wrong one — but the store is visibly not fulfillment-ready.

items.label: Backend verification
items.text: an entered address is validated against the map service before it is accepted, using the same verification path as manager-record addresses. An address arriving via coach import is verified on the same path — imported data is not trusted over typed data.

items.label: Order Fulfillment Mapping
items.text: Shown only for League stores whose fulfillment method is Ship to Team Manager. Mirrors the My Team(s) tab's division/team structure live and maps a freight recipient to every shipping container.

items.label: Per-division mode
items.text: each division routes to the league manager, a single division manager, or individual team managers (with per-team override entries). Manager records collect First/Last Name, Email, 10-digit Phone, and Address — the address is required for order fulfillment. The picker draws on the store's existing manager collection (Epic A2c), so managers named during store creation — or imported from the Team Database — are selectable rather than re-entered.

items.label: Submission gate
items.text: incomplete manager assignments — or a missing destination address on an assigned manager — block pending-order submission (see the Order Management spec). The header shows "n division · m team" assignment counts, and jump-ins from the My Team(s) tab land on Settings → Distribution & Fulfillment with the right division auto-opened (auto-switching it to individual-teams mode when a specific team was targeted).

blocks.heading: Epic A4 — Team Fundraising as a store-level master (General → Store Details)
items: As a rep, I want to see every product I am about to change before I turn fundraising off for the store, so that a one-click switch isn't a blind rewrite of my catalog.
As a rep, I want to be told which items can't have fundraising removed because they've already been ordered, so that I understand why the store isn't fully switched off.
As a rep, I want turning fundraising back on to restore what I had, so that re-enabling isn't a fresh configuration job.

Fundraising is now set per item in the price settings component (see Product Catalog Management (Products Tab), Governing rule 3). The Team Fundraising control on this card is the store-level master over those per-item toggles. It is no longer a boolean, and turning it off is no longer a silent write.

blocks.heading: The control
items: Enabling Team Fundraising makes the Fundraising input available across the catalog, subject to each item's own toggle. New items added after this point default their toggle to on.
Disabling Team Fundraising suppresses fundraising across the catalog — but only through the interstitial below, and never on a commercially-locked item.

items.label: A per-item toggle can always narrow, never widen
items.text: An item's fundraising renders only when the store flag and the item toggle are both on. A rep cannot enable fundraising on one item in a store where fundraising is off.

blocks.heading: The disable interstitial

items.label: Trigger
items.text: Given Team Fundraising is on, when the rep switches it off in the Edit Store Details modal, then an interstitial is presented before the change is applied. The toggle does not take effect until the rep confirms.

items.label: Two lists, not one
items.text: The interstitial has two sections:

items.label: Will be disabled
items.text: every product and bundle in the catalog with fundraising currently enabled, each shown with its name and its current fundraising amount, so the rep can see the scale of what they are switching off rather than a bare count.

items.label: Cannot be disabled
items.text: items exempted by the commercial lock, each with the reason stated plainly: fundraising cannot be removed from an item that has already been ordered. This section is omitted entirely when nothing is exempt.

items: Confirmation copy asks the rep to confirm they want to disable fundraising for the listed products, and states that entered amounts are kept.

items.label: Actions
items.text: Cancel (the toggle reverts, nothing is written) and a confirm action. On confirm, fundraising is disabled for every item in the first list — including items where it was individually enabled — and the exempted items are left untouched.

items.label: Empty case
items.text: where no catalog item has fundraising enabled and none is exempt, the interstitial is skipped and the toggle applies directly. There is nothing to review.

items: This modal is registered in the inventory in System Modals & Toasts.

blocks.heading: Amounts are preserved, on both paths
items: Disabling fundraising — at store level or per item — never clears an entered amount. Figures are stored and reappear intact whenever fundraising is turned back on. The rep is not asked to remember a number they set months ago.
This is deliberately consistent across the two routes: the store-level sweep behaves exactly as a rep flipping each item's toggle by hand would.

blocks.heading: Re-enabling restores prior state
items: Given fundraising was disabled at store level, when the rep re-enables it, then every item returns to the enabled/disabled state it held immediately before the disable, with its preserved amount. Re-enabling is a restore, not a blanket switch-on: an item the rep had individually turned off before the store-level disable comes back off.

blocks.heading: The commercial lock wins
items: An item carrying a non-cancelled order has its fundraising toggle locked along with the rest of its commercial fields (Products Tab, Governing rule 1). The store-level disable cannot override that lock — buyers have already paid the fundraising on those items, and removing it would misstate what the store collected.
The consequence is a legitimate mixed state: Team Fundraising off at store level while ordered items continue to collect. This is expected, not a defect.

items.label: Exempted items re-resolve automatically
items.text: If every order against an exempted item is later cancelled, its commercial lock releases and the store-level disable applies to it from that point.

blocks.heading: Three-state read on the card

State · Pill · Detail line

items.text: Enabled

items.label: Detail line
items.text: Count of catalog items currently collecting

items.label: Pill
items.text: Disabled

items.label: Detail line
items.text: Link into the Products tab filtered to those items

items: This follows the mixed-state pattern already established by the Roster Rules card in Epic F, which reports divergence with a count and a link rather than implying uniformity.

blocks.heading: Epic B — Edit permissions by store state — TBD
items: As a rep, I want to freely edit everything while the store is in draft, so that I can fully dial it in before going live.

items.label: Draft — fully editable
items.text: Given a store in draft mode (created but not yet launched), when the rep opens the Settings tab, then all store settings and information can be edited/changed.

items.label: Launched — partial lock TBD
items.text: Given a launched store, when the rep opens the Settings tab, then a subset of fields becomes non-editable while the rest stay editable.

items.label: OPEN — to be determined
items.text: the exact fields/inputs that lock after launch are TBD and must be defined before build (likely candidates touch fulfillment, tax, format/timeline, and the web address — anything that would disrupt live orders or buyer expectations). The Store Point of Contact is a deliberate exception to lock: contact details must stay editable on a live store so buyers are never pointed at a stale address or a departed manager. The ship-to destination address is a second deliberate exception, for the same reason — a live bulk store must be able to correct where its freight is going. Team Fundraising is a third: it must remain switchable on a launched store, with the commercial lock protecting individual ordered items rather than the store-level control being frozen wholesale. The manager collection is a fourth, for the same reason as the point of contact — coaching changes happen mid-season and must not require a store rebuild. Whether re-binding the store to a different team should be permitted after launch is part of the TBD lock list and should be decided explicitly, since re-binding changes buyer-visible branding on a live storefront.

items: Store Customization & Design is the fifth exception, and both of its controls are exempt from post-launch locking. The Announcement Message exists to communicate order deadlines, returns, sizing, and shipping on a live store; a production date that moves after launch is the ordinary case rather than the exception, and a message frozen at launch is worse than no message because buyers will read it as current. The store theme color is exempt on the same basis — a coach asking for a different color mid-season is a cosmetic change, not a commercial one. Neither control affects pricing, fulfillment, tax, or any placed order, so neither carries the risk the lock list exists to manage. This exemption is not part of the TBD list; it is decided.

blocks.heading: Epic H — Store Close Report
items: As a rep, I want a summary of how a store performed once it closes, so that the result of the season is a moment rather than a spreadsheet.
As a team manager, I want my own version of that summary covering only my team, so that I can see how we did without seeing the rep's margins.
When a store closes, the rep gets a summary of how it performed — presented as a moment rather than left in a reports table.

items.label: Trigger
items.text: generated when the store enters the closed state (Epic D), whether closed manually or by reaching its scheduled close date, and auto-presented on the rep's first return to the workspace after the close.

items.label: Format
items.text: a high-summary, celebratory retrospective — a "year in review" treatment rather than a data table, summarising the closed order window.

items.label: Once, then persistent
items.text: it auto-presents once and is dismissible. Afterward it remains reachable from the Store Status card in Schedule & Status, so the rep can return to it. It gates nothing and blocks no action.

items.label: Team-manager version
items.text: a separate variant is generated for team managers with portal access (Epic A2b), scoped to what that manager can see — their own team's participation and team revenue / fundraising — and made visually distinct from the rep version so the two are never mistaken for each other. It excludes dealer profit and any figure outside that manager's scope. The team-facing figure was formerly team profit; with that input removed (see Products Tab, Governing rule 3), it now reports team revenue and fundraising, matching the Reports tab.

items.label: Re-opening
items.text: if a closed store is re-opened (Epic D) and later closes again, the report regenerates against the new window. The prior report remains available as a record of that earlier window.

items.label: Archiving
items.text: archiving (Epic C) does not generate or regenerate a report. A report already produced stays viewable as part of the archived store's read-only record.

items.label: OPEN — to be confirmed
items.text: the exact metric set on each version. The rep version is expected to cover total raised, orders and units, roster participation, and profit; the manager version a scoped subset. Confirm the figure list — and whether the manager version is emailed on close or only surfaced in-portal — before build.

requirements.subtitle: Epic I — Store Customization & Design
requirements.link: Technical Spec: Store Settings (Settings Tab) — Epic I

blocks.heading: Epic I — Store Customization & Design
items: As a rep, I want somewhere to write the key dates, deadlines, returns, sizing, and shipping information buyers keep asking me about, so that the answers are on the storefront instead of in my text messages.
As a rep, I want to edit that message on a live store, so that a moved production date is a two-minute fix rather than something I cannot change until the window closes.
As a rep running a league, I want a division to be able to carry its own message, so that one division's different deadline doesn't require me to write a message covering every division at once.
As a rep, I want the storefront to pick up my team's color without my doing anything, and to let me change it when the coach asks, so that the default is right and the override is available.

The seventh section. Two cards: the store's storefront accent color, and the announcement message buyers read at the top of the store. The buyer-facing render of both is owned by Storefront Announcement Banner and is not restated here.

items.label: Read view
items.text: Given the section renders, then the current theme color is shown as a swatch with its source — Team default or Custom — so the rep can tell at a glance whether they have overridden anything.

items.label: The picker is Prolook's
items.text: Given the rep opens the color control, then the Prolook color picker component is presented. No bespoke picker is built for this card.

items.label: Default derivation
items.text: Given a store connected to a team, then the theme color defaults to that team's primary color as imported from the Team Database in Step 1 — Basics, Epic D.

items.label: Change Team re-derives a defaulted color
items.text: Given the theme color is still on the team default, when the rep changes the store's connected team (Epic A1), then the color re-derives to the new team's primary color. This is a deliberate departure from the point-in-time-copy pattern that governs coach import — the theme color is a live default, not a snapshot.

items.label: A custom color survives Change Team
items.text: Given the rep has explicitly selected a custom color, when the connected team changes, then the custom color is retained and not overwritten. Re-derivation applies only to values still sitting on the team default. A rep who made a deliberate choice does not have it silently reverted by a branding fix.

items.label: Reset
items.text: Given a custom color, then a Reset to team color action returns the field to the derived default and restores its source label to Team default, re-arming future re-derivation.

items.label: Scope is stated on the card
items.text: Helper copy states that the color applies to buttons and accents only, so the rep is not expecting a full restyle and does not report the unchanged page background as a bug.

items.label: Contrast — OPEN
items.text: Whether the picker warns or blocks on a color with insufficient contrast against button label text is undecided; see the open questions on Storefront Announcement Banner.

items.label: Read view
items.text: Given the section renders, then the current message is shown as rendered rich text, not as markup, with an edit affordance. Given no message, then the empty state states plainly that the storefront shows no banner while the field is empty — the absence is the designed behavior, not an incomplete setup step.

items.label: Editor
items.text: Given the rep edits the message, then a rich-text editor is presented in a focused edit modal, registered in System Modals & Toasts.

items.label: Placeholder guidance
items.text: Given an empty editor, then placeholder text demonstrates the intended use with a worked example covering key dates, order deadlines, returns, sizing, and shipping. The placeholder is illustrative and is never saved as content.

items.label: One field, two surfaces
items.text: Given a message entered in Step 1 — Basics, Epic H, when the rep opens this section, then the same value is present. There is no creation-time copy — the wizard and this card write the same store-level field, consistent with the ship-to address and Team & Roster patterns.

items.label: Live propagation
items.text: Given a launched store, when the message is saved, then the storefront banner reflects it without a republish and without re-opening a closed store.

items.label: Free text, and the rep owns its accuracy
items.text: The message is not parsed, date-checked, or reconciled against the store's configured ordering window. A rep may type a deadline that differs from the countdown on the Ordering-Window Banner, and the system will not detect or warn about it. This is an accepted consequence of a free-text field.

items.label: Character limit and permitted marks — OPEN
items.text: A ceiling on message length and the permitted rich-text feature set (in particular whether links are allowed) are undecided and implementation-blocking; see the open questions on Storefront Announcement Banner.

blocks.heading: League stores: per-division and per-standalone-team overrides

items.label: Conditional surface
items.text: Given a League Store, then the section additionally lists the store's divisions and standalone teams, each with an optional announcement message. Given an Individual Team Store, then no override surface is present — there is no division tier and one team.

items.label: Override granularity is division and standalone team only
items.text: A team inside a division does not carry its own message; it inherits its division's. This is the deliberate boundary on the feature's complexity.

items.label: Inheriting is shown as inheriting
items.text: Given a division or standalone team carrying no message, then the read view shows it as inheriting the store-level message, not as empty — the same mixed-state honesty the Roster Rules card applies in Epic F.

items.label: Division color reuse — no second color field
items.text: Given a division, then its color contribution is the existing division brand color set in the My Team(s) tab detail panel. This section offers a per-division toggle to apply the division's brand color to the storefront for shoppers resolved to that division, and links out to My Team(s) to change the color itself. No division-specific color is stored here.

items.label: Deleting a division drops its customization
items.text: Given a division carrying a message or an applied color is deleted, when its teams become standalone, then they drop both along with the division's branding and resolve to store level unless they carry their own — matching the existing delete semantics in Roster-Optional Architecture, Epic B.

items.label: Ergonomics for large leagues
items.text: the override list is searchable with multi-select bulk apply, mirroring the Order Window Scheduler's ergonomics. It does not mirror its key — see Epic E.

items.label: Resolution is a storefront concern
items.text: How a shopper is matched to a division or team, and the fallback order when they are matched to neither, is specified in Storefront Announcement Banner, Epic C, and keys off the team selector in Roster-Optional Architecture, Epic D.

children.caption: Store Theme Color card
items: As a rep, I want the storefront to pick up my team's color without my doing anything, and to let me change it when the coach asks, so that the default is right and the override is available.

items.label: Read view
items.text: Given the section renders, then the current theme color is shown as a swatch with its source — Team default or Custom — so the rep can tell at a glance whether they have overridden anything.

items.label: The picker is Prolook's
items.text: Given the rep opens the color control, then the Prolook color picker component is presented. No bespoke picker is built for this card.

items.label: Default derivation
items.text: Given a store connected to a team, then the theme color defaults to that team's primary color as imported from the Team Database in Step 1 — Basics, Epic D.

items.label: Change Team re-derives a defaulted color
items.text: Given the theme color is still on the team default, when the rep changes the store's connected team (Epic A1), then the color re-derives to the new team's primary color. This is a deliberate departure from the point-in-time-copy pattern that governs coach import — the theme color is a live default, not a snapshot.

items.label: A custom color survives Change Team
items.text: Given the rep has explicitly selected a custom color, when the connected team changes, then the custom color is retained and not overwritten. Re-derivation applies only to values still sitting on the team default. A rep who made a deliberate choice does not have it silently reverted by a branding fix.

items.label: Reset
items.text: Given a custom color, then a Reset to team color action returns the field to the derived default and restores its source label to Team default, re-arming future re-derivation.

items.label: Scope is stated on the card
items.text: Helper copy states that the color applies to buttons and accents only, so the rep is not expecting a full restyle and does not report the unchanged page background as a bug.

items.label: Contrast — OPEN
items.text: Whether the picker warns or blocks on a color with insufficient contrast against button label text is undecided; see the open questions on Storefront Announcement Banner.

children.caption: Announcement Message card & editor modal
items: As a rep, I want somewhere to write the key dates, deadlines, returns, sizing, and shipping information buyers keep asking me about, so that the answers are on the storefront instead of in my text messages.
As a rep, I want to edit that message on a live store, so that a moved production date is a two-minute fix rather than something I cannot change until the window closes.

items.label: Read view
items.text: Given the section renders, then the current message is shown as rendered rich text, not as markup, with an edit affordance. Given no message, then the empty state states plainly that the storefront shows no banner while the field is empty — the absence is the designed behavior, not an incomplete setup step.

items.label: Editor
items.text: Given the rep edits the message, then a rich-text editor is presented in a focused edit modal, registered in System Modals & Toasts.

items.label: Placeholder guidance
items.text: Given an empty editor, then placeholder text demonstrates the intended use with a worked example covering key dates, order deadlines, returns, sizing, and shipping. The placeholder is illustrative and is never saved as content.

items.label: One field, two surfaces
items.text: Given a message entered in Step 1 — Basics, Epic H, when the rep opens this section, then the same value is present. There is no creation-time copy — the wizard and this card write the same store-level field, consistent with the ship-to address and Team & Roster patterns.

items.label: Live propagation
items.text: Given a launched store, when the message is saved, then the storefront banner reflects it without a republish and without re-opening a closed store.

items.label: Free text, and the rep owns its accuracy
items.text: The message is not parsed, date-checked, or reconciled against the store's configured ordering window. A rep may type a deadline that differs from the countdown on the Ordering-Window Banner, and the system will not detect or warn about it. This is an accepted consequence of a free-text field.

items.label: Character limit and permitted marks — OPEN
items.text: A ceiling on message length and the permitted rich-text feature set (in particular whether links are allowed) are undecided and implementation-blocking; see the open questions on Storefront Announcement Banner.

children.caption: League division / standalone-team override list
items: As a rep running a league, I want a division to be able to carry its own message, so that one division's different deadline doesn't require me to write a message covering every division at once.

items.label: Conditional surface
items.text: Given a League Store, then the section additionally lists the store's divisions and standalone teams, each with an optional announcement message. Given an Individual Team Store, then no override surface is present — there is no division tier and one team.

items.label: Override granularity is division and standalone team only
items.text: A team inside a division does not carry its own message; it inherits its division's. This is the deliberate boundary on the feature's complexity.

items.label: Inheriting is shown as inheriting
items.text: Given a division or standalone team carrying no message, then the read view shows it as inheriting the store-level message, not as empty — the same mixed-state honesty the Roster Rules card applies in Epic F.

items.label: Division color reuse — no second color field
items.text: Given a division, then its color contribution is the existing division brand color set in the My Team(s) tab detail panel. This section offers a per-division toggle to apply the division's brand color to the storefront for shoppers resolved to that division, and links out to My Team(s) to change the color itself. No division-specific color is stored here.

items.label: Deleting a division drops its customization
items.text: Given a division carrying a message or an applied color is deleted, when its teams become standalone, then they drop both along with the division's branding and resolve to store level unless they carry their own — matching the existing delete semantics in Roster-Optional Architecture, Epic B.

items.label: Ergonomics for large leagues
items.text: the override list is searchable with multi-select bulk apply, mirroring the Order Window Scheduler's ergonomics. It does not mirror its key — see Epic E.

items.label: Resolution is a storefront concern
items.text: How a shopper is matched to a division or team, and the fallback order when they are matched to neither, is specified in Storefront Announcement Banner, Epic C, and keys off the team selector in Roster-Optional Architecture, Epic D.

blocks.heading: Metrics & Success Criteria
items: Store edits made without recreating a store
Setting-change error rate near zero
Time-to-find for a given setting (seven-section nav vs. the prior two-section layout)
Post-launch edit attempts blocked on locked fields (once defined)
Share of stores keeping the Team Manager point-of-contact default vs. switching to Salesperson or Custom
Manager-record edits that correctly propagate to the storefront footer — target 100%
Managers per store, and share of stores changing their primary manager after launch

Manager records added post-launch by coach import vs. by hand — the read on whether the Team Database path is reachable from where reps actually go to add a manager, and the input to the OPEN question about surfacing it on the manager card
Re-binds that leave managers from the previous team, and the split between keeping and removing them — a read on whether the prompt is set at the right default
Re-binds where a left-behind manager held active portal access — the failure case the callout exists to prevent; the metric to watch is whether reps then go to People & Access and act
Ship-to destination addresses added here after launch — the recovery path for stores that skipped it at creation, and a read on how often creation-time capture is being skipped
Destination-address clears followed by a re-entry within the same session — a read on whether clearing is being used for correction (expected) or by mistake
Share of destinations here resolving to a saved Pick-up Location vs. a typed address, and stores left without a destination after a location was switched off at workspace level
Fundraising disable interstitials cancelled vs. confirmed — a high cancel rate means the sweep was larger than the rep expected, which is exactly what the interstitial exists to reveal
Stores sitting in the disabled-with-exemptions mixed state, and how long they stay there

Store-level fundraising disables followed by a re-enable within 30 days — a read on whether the master switch is being used to explore rather than to decide, and on whether state restoration is doing real work
Bulk duplicate-number applies per store, and share of rosters subsequently overriding — a read on whether the bulk default is set to the right value
Share of stores whose Team & Roster values were set at creation and never edited here — a read on whether the creation-time panel is doing its job
Share of live stores carrying a non-empty announcement message — the read on whether reps treat this as setup, as research suggested
Announcement messages entered at creation (Step 1 Epic H) vs. added here after the fact — a read on whether the wizard panel is placed where reps will use it
Announcement message edits on launched stores, and time from launch to first edit — the metric that justifies the Epic B lock exemption; a write-once pattern would suggest the exemption is unused
Share of League stores using division or standalone-team overrides vs. store-level only — whether override granularity earns its complexity
Share of stores overriding the default theme color vs. accepting the team primary color, and share of overrides that are later reset to the team color
Theme colors retained through a Change Team — confirmation that a custom choice is surviving a re-bind as specified
Scheduled vs. manual closures; re-open rate
Store Close Report view rate on first return after close; share of reps re-opening it later
Manager-version close report views per store with an active team manager
Total raised per pop-up window; orders in final days; per-team-code window coverage gaps resolved
Team-manager invites sent / activated / revoked per store, and share sent against an existing manager record rather than a fresh address
Archived stores retained as read-only records
Manager-mapping completeness for Ship-to-Team-Manager League stores (freight-gate readiness)

requirements.name: Dependencies & Technical Constraints
requirements.link: Technical Spec: Store Settings (Settings Tab) — Dependencies & Technical Constraints

blocks.heading: Dependency & Technical Constraint
items: Reuses the entire Step 1 — Basics field set and validation (Team Database pull for logo/colors/sports/coaches, salesperson/contact directory, scheduling persistence, and the Collect Sales Tax toggle with its searchable state select, state→flat-rate lookup, and liability agreement), split across per-card edit modals (Store Details, League/Team Manager Information, Fulfillment Method, Edit Store Schedule, Store Theme Color, Announcement Message) under a seven-section Settings layout driven by a single section key — deep links from elsewhere in the workspace (e.g. My Team(s) → manager mapping) must target the correct section id, and adding a section must not renumber or invalidate existing section keys. The Edit Store Details modal owns Team Branding & Sport (connect-to-team re-binding with branding re-import and coach import), the Roster Rules and Team Fundraising toggles, Compliance & Taxation, and the Store Point of Contact; the manager card holds the manager collection's names, addresses, phones, emails, and contact preferences.

Coach import requires the Team Database connect to return the coach records attached to the selected team or organization in the same payload as the branding. Imported coaches are written into the same manager collection as hand-entered records — no separate entity, no parallel table, no origin-based behavior in any downstream consumer. The import is a point-in-time copy with no live binding in either direction: manager edits never write back to the Team Database, and Team Database changes never mutate an existing store's records. Re-binding requires the connect to resolve which existing manager records originated from the team being replaced, which means retaining a source-team reference on imported records; hand-entered records carry none and are excluded from the re-bind prompt. Resolving that set must also join against the People & Access invite table so records with active or pending access can be called out. The Team Database coach schema — specifically whether records carry a mailing address and a role or title — is an open dependency (see Step 1 — Basics, Epic D2 and Epic F).

Import must carry no access-granting side effect. No account, invite, entitlement, or notification may be created by importing a coach, and no code path may infer portal access from the presence of a manager record. Conversely, deleting a manager record must not revoke an invite. The manager collection and the invite table are independent, and every surface that touches both must state the consequence rather than resolve it silently.

Team Fundraising is no longer a boolean store field. It requires: a catalog-wide read returning every product and bundle with fundraising enabled, together with its current amount, to populate the disable interstitial; an exemption pass resolving which of those items carry a non-cancelled order and are therefore protected by the commercial lock; a bulk write that clears the per-item flag across the non-exempt set on confirm; amount preservation so no write ever clears a stored fundraising figure; prior-state retention capturing each item's own flag at the moment of a store-level disable so that re-enabling restores rather than switches on; and a three-state resolution — enabled, disabled, disabled-with-exemptions — consumed by the Store Details pill, by the Fundraising Report's render gate (Store Analytics (Reports Tab), Epic D), and by the price settings component's conditional Fundraising column (Products Tab, Governing rule 3). Exemption status must re-resolve automatically when an item's orders are all cancelled, releasing it to the store-level setting. Team Fundraising must be excluded from the post-launch lock list.

Store Customization & Design requires a store-level theme color field carrying its own source flag (team-derived vs. rep-selected) — the flag is not inferrable from the value, since a rep may legitimately pick the same color the team default would have produced, and re-derivation on Change Team depends on knowing which it is. Re-derivation must be wired into the connect-to-team save path in Epic A1 and must fire only where the source flag reads team-derived. The color is consumed through token-level indirection scoped to buttons and accents; it must not be implemented as a global brand-color override, so that the blast radius is bounded by the token set rather than by a stylesheet search.

It also requires a store-level announcement message field holding sanitized rich text, written by this card and by Step 1 — Basics Epic H against the same persisted value with no creation-time copy, plus optional announcement message fields on division and standalone-team structure records as specified in Roster-Optional Architecture, Epic B. Teams inside a division carry no such field. The division's color contribution is the existing division brand color and introduces no new storage. Deleting a division must drop its announcement message and applied-color flag on the same path that already drops its branding. Rich text requires a sanitizing renderer on the storefront — script, embed, iframe, and event-handler content stripped rather than escaped-and-displayed — and the editor must not be treated as a trusted-input boundary merely because the author is a rep. Both controls must be excluded from the post-launch lock list, and the storefront must read live store state so a mid-window edit propagates without a republish. The override list's bulk-apply must write per division and per standalone team; it must not reuse the Order Window Scheduler's per-team-code write path.

The manager card requires a collection of manager records with exactly one designated primary, writable from this card, from Step 1 — Basics Epic E, and from coach import, all against the same persisted collection. Primary designation drives point-of-contact inheritance and is the only record subject to point-of-contact validation; re-designation must repoint the live storefront footer without a store re-save, and removal of the primary must be blocked until another is designated — including when the removal originates from the re-bind prompt. Manager records must carry no access-granting side effect — portal entitlement is created only by an invite record in People & Access.

The Store Point of Contact requires a per-channel mode persisted independently for Email and Phone and a live binding to the primary manager record so contact edits propagate to the storefront footer without re-saving the store, plus a blank-value guard at save. That binding is internal to Team Stores and does not extend to the Team Database.

The ship-to destination address must be a single persisted field shared by three surfaces — Step 1 — Basics Epic F, the Fulfillment Method card here, and the primary manager record — never a wizard-local value copied forward. It requires the same backend map-service verification as manager-record addresses, applied equally to addresses arriving via coach import, a clearable state that saves successfully while reporting the store as not fulfillment-ready, and consumption by the pending-order freight gate so a cleared or missing address blocks submission rather than shipping to nowhere. Where the destination is supplied as a saved Pick-up Location, it must be held as a reference to that location rather than a copy of its address, so a workspace-level edit propagates and a location switched off leaves the store detectably without a destination (Pick Up Locations, Governing rule 3 and Epic C); reading the saved-location list requires the workspace-scoped location service, and a workspace with no locations must render the manual path with no error. It must be excluded from the post-launch lock list.

Allow Duplicate Numbers must be implemented here as a bulk write across the store's rosters plus a mixed-state read, not as a parent value inherited at read time — the authoritative value lives on each roster (Roster Management, Epic 4), and new rosters read this control only at creation, including rosters created during store creation. Jersey number selection writes a store-level mode consumed by both the roster editor and the buyer product page. Both values are written by Step 1 — Basics Epic D1 to the same store-level fields these cards read; no duplicate creation-time storage may exist.

People & Access requires store-scoped invite records with status/last-login, an email-invite + password-set flow, a revoke path that also withdraws close-report access, an impersonation ("View portal as") entry into the two-area Team Manager Portal, and a read of the manager collection so an invite can be sent against an existing record's email — imported and hand-entered alike. The Order Fulfillment Mapping requires the shared roster-org state (divisions / standalone teams mirrored live with the My Team(s) tab), per-division fulfillment modes, manager records with required addresses selected from the store's manager collection, and the freight gate consumed by pending-order submission. The Order Window Scheduler needs per-team-code window persistence with timezones, bulk apply, and gap analysis.

The Store Close Report requires a close-triggered aggregation job over the completed order window (revenue, orders, units, roster participation, profit split, top products), a generated-report record per close event so re-opening and re-closing produces a new report without destroying the prior one, a seen/dismissed flag per rep driving the auto-present-once behavior on next workspace entry, a persistent entry point on the Store Status card, and a manager-scoped projection of the same aggregation that excludes dealer profit and any out-of-scope figures, gated on active team-manager access. The manager projection's team-facing figure reads team revenue and fundraising, not team profit, which no longer exists. Archiving must not trigger generation, and archived stores must retain existing reports as read-only.

Adds a store-state-aware edit-permission layer: in draft every field is writable; once launched, a TBD subset of fields is locked (the lock list must be finalized before build), with the Store Point of Contact, the ship-to destination address, Team Fundraising, the manager collection, and both Store Customization & Design controls explicitly excluded from locking, and the re-bind action's post-launch availability an explicit open item. Archiving requires an owner-scoped state transition that disables the public storefront route (serving a neutral "store closed" screen) and flips the management dashboard to read-only while retaining all records — undoable only by support. Closing is a separate reversible state (manual or triggered by the scheduled close date) that locks the storefront behind a "This store is closed" page while keeping the workspace fully editable; storefront changes only go live on a manual re-open. The Active Order Window card + Edit Store Schedule modal require an aggregate of order revenue raised during the window and a countdown derived from the store's open/close dates (rendered for always-on stores as an "Always open" state). Catalog & Decoration is gated on a per-store third-party vendor enabled flag; when false, neither the section nor its nav entry is rendered. Database updates + shared internal team / tax services.
